newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says it killed Eritrean forces in east.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says it killed Eritrean forces in east.

text.p: Sudan on Friday said its army killed more than 60 Eritrean soldiers and seized a large amount of arms in the eastern state of Kassala where rebels claim to have made advances in their insurgency against Khartoum.
Sudan accuses neighbouring Eritrea and Ethiopia of orchestrating the fighting. Both countries, which host Sudanese rebels, reject the allegations.

The Sudanese government-owned al-Ingaz al-Watani newspaper quoted government spokesman Brigadier al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair as saying Sudanese forces had killed 63 Eritrean soldiers. He did not say when.

President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, in a radio broadcast on Thursday night, vowed to stand strong against the attacks while convoys of government soldiers, members of the paramilitary Popular Defence Forces and volunteers headed for Kassala and the southeastern Blue Nile state.

The Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said on Friday a joint rebel force had captured the town of Maban on the southern front of the Blue Nile region and that it was advancing on Damazin and its hydro-electric power station.
Damazin is about 480 km (300 miles) southeast of Khartoum and supplies Khartoum with up to 80 percent of its power.
The rebels say they have already seized two towns on the border with Ethiopia -- Kurmuk and Qeissan.

Khair denied rebel claims that they had captured a Sudanese military garrison at Gadamyeeb, northeast of Kassala town which is close to the Eritrean border and lies about 280 miles (450 km) east of the Sudanese capital.

Northern and southern rebels working together in their first combined offensive to overthrow Khartoum's Islamist government say they are responsible for the attacks against army units in the east, which began earlier this week.
The rebels say their objective is not to capture the capital but to strangle it and provoke an uprising against Bashir's Islamist military government.
Bashir accused Ethiopia and Eritrea of coordinating the attacks to topple his government and vowed to stand strong.

"What is going on in the eastern front is a Zionist, imperialist plot being implemented by Eritrea and Ethiopia aimed at setting up a secular, African state in Sudan instead of the present state," said Bashir, a lieutenant-general who seized power in a coup in 1989.
"Sudan will face off any attack as a duty to our religion and nation," Bashir said. He said he did not rule out an attack on the entire length of Sudan's eastern front.
Defence Minister Hasan Abdel-Rahman Ali and Federal Rule Minister Ali al-Haj Mohammad arrived in Damazin on Thursday to inspect government troops, Sudanese radio reported.
It said Mohammad chaired an emergency meeting of the Blue Nile State government "to review the situation in the state following the Ethiopian aggression against it."
Omdurman Ahlia University closed on Thursday because of the fighting. Khartoum University closed earlier this week to allow students and workers there to volunteer for the front.
